blocks.text: Quito, Ecuador: churches and rooftops in the historic centre, with a hill and mountains beyond

Set out early. At 07:00, take a speedboat to Isabela Island. The crossing takes about 2 hours.

Arrive at the main dock in Puerto Villamil, the island’s only small town, then head to the wetlands. Several species of mangrove grow here, and a network of small lagoons winds through volcanic formations. Flamingos, black-necked stilts and other birds can be seen here. The contrast between black lava, mangroves and water shows how varied the habitats of the Galápagos can be.

Continue to the visitor centre to learn about the work of Galápagos National Park and its efforts to protect native species.

After lunch at a local restaurant, continue to Las Tintoreras. This small islet lies south of Puerto Villamil in a bay with turquoise water. You may see sea lions, sea turtles, marine iguanas and rays. Reef sharks rest in channels between the lava rocks, where you can watch for them on a short walk across the solidified lava.

Return to Puerto Ayora at around 17:00 and stay at the 4-star Villa Laguna hotel.

Meals: breakfast and lunch.
White sand and black volcanic rocks on the shore of Isabela Island, Galápagos, Ecuador
Isabela Island: turquoise water beside a pale sandy beach and dark rocks
Charles Darwin Research Station and Tortuga Bay

In the morning, visit the Charles Darwin Research Station. Its exhibits cover the history and development of the Galápagos Islands and efforts to protect the archipelago’s natural heritage. At the station, you can see endemic giant tortoises and learn about the programmes that help protect their populations. Several species live across the archipelago, and the station studies and protects them.

A separate exhibit is devoted to Lonesome George, the last of his subspecies. He died in 2012, and the subspecies became extinct. His preserved body is kept at the station.

In the afternoon, head to Tortuga Bay. Walk from the hotel through a cactus forest. The first stretch of coast, Playa Brava, is known for its strong currents, so the visit here focuses on walking along the shore and watching wildlife. Marine iguanas, pelicans and other birds can be seen on the sand and among the rocks. Walk about 15 minutes farther to Playa Mansa, a calm natural lagoon where you may see blue-footed boobies and pelicans. You can swim, sunbathe and relax by the water.

Walk to Tortuga Bay and return by boat. Lunch is not included today. Your guide will recommend a restaurant.

Return to the 4-star Villa Laguna hotel after the excursion. The evening is free.

Meals: breakfast.
